questions.question: What are the two types of telework?
questions.answer: The two types of telework are situational (unscheduled) and routine (regular and recurring).

citations.quote: There are two types of telework: situational (unscheduled) and routine (regular and recurring).

questions.question: On what date was the Presidential Memorandum on returning to in-person work signed?
questions.answer: The Presidential Memorandum on returning to in-person work was signed on January 20, 2025.

citations.quote: On January 20, 2025, President Donald J. Trump signed a Presidential Memorandum (PM) titled, Return to In-Person Work

questions.question: What is situational telework?
questions.answer: Situational telework, also referred to as unscheduled, episodic, intermittent, or ad-hoc telework, allows employees to work from an alternative location on an occasional, episodic, or short-term basis. It is approved on a case-by-case basis and does not form part of an ongoing or regular telework schedule.

citations.quote: Situational Telework An agency may permit employees to perform situational telework, also known as unscheduled telework, that allows employees to telework on an occasional, episodic, or short- term basis.

questions.question: Which public law is the Telework Enhancement Act?
questions.answer: The Telework Enhancement Act is Public Law 111-292, enacted on December 9, 2010.

citations.quote: The Telework Enhancement Act (Public Law 111-292, December 9, 2010)

questions.question: What is the official worksite for an employee who has a signed telework agreement?
questions.answer: For most employees who have a signed telework agreement, the official worksite is the agency worksite.

citations.quote: Official worksite is the agency worksite for most employees, including an employee with a signed telework agreement.

questions.question: What must a federal employee complete before entering a written telework agreement?
questions.answer: Before entering into a written telework agreement, employees are required to successfully complete telework training.

citations.quote: Additionally, employees are required to successfully complete telework training before entering a written telework agreement.

questions.question: What role must each agency designate as its primary point of contact for OPM on telework matters?
questions.answer: Each agency must designate an employee as its Telework Managing Officer (TMO) to act as the primary point of contact for OPM regarding telework matters.

citations.quote: each agency must designate an employee of the agency as its Telework Managing Officer (TMO) to serve as the primary agency point of contact for OPM on telework matters.

questions.question: When was NIST CSF 2.0 published?
questions.answer: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0 was published on February 26, 2024.

citations.quote: February 26, 2024 The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0

questions.question: What are the six Functions of the CSF Core?
questions.answer: The six Functions of the CSF Core are GOVERN, IDENTIFY, PROTECT, DETECT, RESPOND, and RECOVER.

citations.quote: The CSF Core Functions — GOVERN, IDENTIFY, PROTECT, DETECT, RESPOND, and RECOVER — organize cybersecurity outcomes at their highest level.

questions.question: What are the four CSF Tiers?
questions.answer: The four CSF Tiers are Partial (Tier 1), Risk Informed (Tier 2), Repeatable (Tier 3), and Adaptive (Tier 4).

citations.quote: There are four Tiers: Partial (Tier 1), Risk Informed (Tier 2), Repeatable (Tier 3), and Adaptive (Tier 4).

questions.question: What is the CSF Core?
questions.answer: The CSF Core is a set of cybersecurity outcomes arranged hierarchically by Function, Category, and Subcategory. These outcomes detail specific aspects of cybersecurity and are designed to resonate with those responsible for operationalizing risk management within an organization. The Core components can be understood by a broad audience regardless of their cybersecurity expertise and are sector-, country-, and technology-neutral to provide flexibility.

citations.quote: Appendix A is the CSF Core — a set of cybersecurity outcomes arranged by Function, then Category, and finally Subcategory
The CSF Core components are a hierarchy of Functions, Categories, and Subcategories that detail each outcome.

questions.question: Which two topics do the new features of CSF 2.0 highlight?
questions.answer: CSF 2.0 contains new features that highlight the importance of governance and supply chains.

citations.quote: Building on previous versions, CSF 2.0 contains new features tha t highlight the importance of governance and supply chains.

questions.question: Who is the primary audience for the CSF?
questions.answer: Individuals who are responsible for developing and leading cybersecurity programs serve as the primary audience for the CSF.

citations.quote: Individuals responsible for developing and leading cybersecurity programs are the primary audience for the CSF.

questions.question: What is a CSF Community Profile?
questions.answer: A Community Profile is a baseline of CSF outcomes created and published to address shared interests and goals among a number of organizations. It is typically developed for a particular sector, subsector, technology, threat type, or other use case, and can be used by an organization as the basis for its own Target Profile.

citations.quote: A Community Profile is a baseline of CSF outcomes that is created and published to address shared interests and goals among a number of organizations.
